title: AWS Lambda consumer for self-managed Apache Kafka with IAM Outbound (SASL/OAUTHBEARER) auth (Java)
description: Creates a Lambda function that consumes from a self-managed Apache Kafka cluster on EC2, secured with SASL/OAUTHBEARER using AWS IAM Outbound Identity Federation (no external IdP) - the poller and clients present AWS-minted web-identity tokens.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern provisions a self-managed Apache Kafka cluster (3 brokers on 3 EC2 instances, KRaft mode) plus a 4th EC2 instance that acts as a Kafka client and SAM deployment host.

The Kafka brokers are configured for SASL/OAUTHBEARER, validating AWS-minted web-identity (OIDC) tokens against the AWS STS Outbound Identity Federation JWKS endpoint, with a required audience. There is no external identity provider.

The Lambda event source poller mints a web-identity token from its execution role (sts:GetWebIdentityToken) and presents it to the brokers. The interactive admin/producer/consumer clients assume dedicated IAM roles and mint their own tokens, so Kafka ACLs still distinguish them.

This deploys via the AWS CLI (deploy_lambda_oauth_cli.sh) using IAM_OAUTHBEARER_AUTH + OAUTHBEARER_AUDIENCE, since AWS SAM does not support these event-source auth types yet. This is an under-development capability.
For detailed deployment instructions see the README.md
